name: Hannah Hewitt
life: “I still remember an orange sandal caught against the rocks.” People around Juniper Street know Hannah by a small Wednesday habit. Hannah knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I remember the girl standing on one foot. She was waiting for her other sandal to wash back.
appearance: Hannah has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a little coil of soft measuring tape. When somebody else has the floor, Hannah looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Hannah feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To trace the missing sandal's owner.
family: Terry Perry is Hannah’s stepsibling. Hannah saves a place. Terry chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Terry says, “I am her partner. We picked one word she can say when she's ready to get back in the car.”
connections: Charlotte Bruno. They tell a child why a bare foot stayed still on that particular day.

reactions.situation: A visitor insists the footprint must belong to a famous runner
reactions.response: Hannah checks for a family photograph before accepting the famous name.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Hannah brings the worker into the conversation and asks what they remember without feeding them a story.

reactions.situation: If an argument gets loud at home
